Microsoft installed Windows defender at OpenAI




Muskonomy (@muskonomy)

BREAKING: OpenAI board observer from Microsoft was not part of sensitive discussions, Bret Taylor says

Dee Templeton, a Microsoft corporate vice president and deputy chief technology officer, served as an observer on OpenAI's nonprofit board after Sam Altman's brief ouster in November 2023.

OpenAI Chairman Bret Taylor confirmed this in court today under questioning from Jay Jurata, a Dechert lawyer representing Microsoft in the Musk v. Altman trial.

Templeton attended one or two board meetings. She had no voting rights and did not take part in competitively sensitive discussions, Taylor said.

Taylor added that he was not sure why Templeton was given the spot, but understood Microsoft wanting representation given that "the company had recently almost imploded."

Microsoft is the largest investor in OpenAI's for-profit arm with over $13 billion committed. Even a brief seat at the nonprofit table strengthens Musk's argument that Microsoft had outsized influence over the supposedly independent charity.
